ingredients.name_en: fresh onion or spring onion, sliced

steps: Soak the bread in a bowl of cold water — it must be Tuscan bread, ideally wood-oven baked and a bit stale; let sit 30 minutes in the refrigerator to reconstitute.
Squeeze out the water; repeat 3 or 4 times.
Place in a large serving bowl and cover with all the other ingredients.
Dress with salt, oil, and a little vinegar; mix well.
Let rest for half an hour; taste and adjust oil or vinegar before serving.
Remove the tough outer leaves, stem, and the tips of the artichokes.
Spread the leaves and place artichokes in a bowl with water and lemon juice.
Prepare the filling by mixing the breadcrumbs with garlic, parsley, salt, pepper, and oil.
Fill the artichokes with the stuffing; place them in a pan with a little oil and two glasses of water.
Cover and cook on the stovetop for 30–40 minutes.
Peel the vegetables and cut into pieces.
In a saucepan, sauté the garlic with 2 tablespoons of oil and a little water.
Add eggplants and bell peppers; cook for 5 minutes.
Add tomatoes, potatoes, and zucchini; season with salt, oregano, and basil leaves.
Simmer, stirring occasionally; if needed, add water or vegetable broth.
Peel the potatoes, cut into slices, and blanch them in salted water until half cooked.
Cut bell peppers into big pieces and brown them in a pan with 2 tablespoons of oil.
Remove the bell peppers and discard the used oil.
With fresh oil, cook the tomatoes cut into pieces.
When the tomato juices have evaporated, add the bell peppers and potatoes; cook uncovered.
Season with salt and serve warm.
Clean the squid and cuttlefish, cut into small pieces, and let drain.
Fry the garlic in the oil; add the squid and cuttlefish and sauté on medium heat.
Add tomatoes cut in small pieces, salt, and pepper; cook a few more minutes.
Sprinkle with parsley and serve.
Peel the endive, cut into strips, and soak in water for a few minutes.
Remove the anchovy heads and clean the fish, opening like a book; wash and dry them.
Drain the endive and put a third in a casserole dish.
Cover with half of the anchovies and season with oil, garlic, salt, and pepper.
Continue with a second layer of endive and the rest of the anchovies; season; top with the remaining endive.
Bake at 200 °C / 400 °F for 30 minutes.
Serve warm, sprinkled with chopped parsley.
Cook the onions in salted water; drain and set aside.
Crush the walnuts and garlic in a mortar with a pinch of salt until everything becomes a paste.
Add the oil and lemon juice gradually.
Finish the sauce with chopped parsley.
Serve the onions in large pieces, topped with the sauce.
Briefly blanch the outer leaves of the cabbage in salted boiling water and drain.
Soak the bread in water, wring it out, and mix in the chopped parsley, salt, pepper, and a little oil.
Knead and divide the bread mixture into flattened patties.
Cover each patty with cabbage leaves and fix with a toothpick.
Dredge the patties in corn flour and bake in a hot oven for 20 minutes.
Prepare a sauce with chopped garlic and onion, then add tomato and the rest of the cabbage cut into strips.
After a few minutes, add the patties; cook briefly and serve. Remove the toothpicks before serving.
Cut the vegetables into large pieces and cook at low heat with a little water, adding salt as desired.
After 30 minutes, pass the mixture through a vegetable mill or use an immersion blender; the soup should be thick.
Serve hot, seasoned with olive oil, pepper, and sage.
Clean the fish, removing the scales and entrails. Wash and dry well.
Place in an oiled baking dish.
Add pepper, olives, and tomatoes previously crushed by hand.
Bake at 160 °C / 320 °F for 30 minutes, basting with the wine halfway through cooking.
Soak the chickpeas overnight and the spelt for a couple of hours.
Boil the chickpeas; drain them and keep the cooking water.
In a pan, brown the chopped onion, carrot, and celery in oil.
Add the drained chickpeas, drained spelt, and 2 liters of the chickpea cooking water.
Finish cooking at medium heat for 40 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Salt to taste; serve with olive oil and fresh ground pepper.

recipes.name_en: Sweet and Sour Sardines (Sarde in Saor)
steps: Remove the sardine heads, scales, and entrails.
Flour the sardines and fry them for a few minutes.
Brown the onions in a cup of water and a tablespoon of oil.
Add vinegar, raisins, and pine nuts; cook for 10 minutes.
Arrange the sardines alternating with onions in a bowl; cover with the cooking liquid and store in a cool place.
After two days, the sardines are ready to eat and will keep for up to a week.
Pour the semolina into a deep dish and wet it with a bit of cold water; mix well, rolling the mixture with your hand in one direction and then the other until granules form.
Add salt, pepper, oil, and one finely minced onion; let rest about 10 minutes.
Fill a pot with water; add the bay leaves, a small piece of onion, parsley, and salt. On top, place the couscous pot containing the seasoned semolina.
Make a sheet of dough using water and the wheat flour; place it between the pot and the couscous pot to seal.
Cook on a low flame for an hour and a half.
Prepare the fish stew: heat the oil; add the crushed garlic, the remaining minced onion, the almonds, and parsley.
After a few minutes add the tomatoes and 2 liters of lightly salted water; when the broth boils, add the fish; cook for 30 minutes.
Remove the fish and keep hot; filter the broth through a fine sieve.
Place the couscous in a large bowl, ladle in some of the broth, and let rest covered for 30 minutes.
Serve in individual shallow bowls with pieces of fish on top; serve the remaining broth on the side as a condiment.
Soak the chickpeas in water overnight, then boil; keep the cooking liquid.
Blend the chickpeas to a creamy puree.
Add the lemon juice and 2 tablespoons of the cooking water a little at a time while blending.
Add the tahini and garlic; continue to blend, adding a bit of salt.
Transfer to a bowl; drizzle with oil and dust with paprika and parsley.
To make tahini at home: toast sesame seeds 5 minutes in a non-stick pan, stirring carefully; transfer to a food processor with oil and puree until smooth.

recipes.name_en: Roasted Yellow Peppers with Anchovies, Capers, Garlic, Basil, Herbs

ingredients.name_en: aromatic herbs mix (parsley, sage, marjoram, mint, summer savory, thyme, celery leaves, arugula, tarragon)

steps: Roast the peppers over a flame, peel, and cut into quarters; dry and place on a tray.
Rinse the anchovies and capers of their salt.
On each pepper strip place 2 anchovy filets, 2 slices of garlic, then the capers.
Mince the herbs and mix with the minced garlic.
Remove the garlic from the peppers and cover with the herb mixture.
Spread torn basil leaves over the peppers and serve.

recipes.name_en: Salad with Anchovies, Hardboiled Eggs, Tomatoes, Cucumber, Peppers, Olives
steps: Rinse the anchovies of their salt, debone, and soak in a bowl of vinegar for 10 minutes.
Dry with a cloth and line up on a plate with oil, alongside a clove of crushed garlic and some chili pepper.
Wet the taralli somewhat in salted water; spray with vinegar and dry for 5 minutes with a dish cloth.
Wash and dry the tomatoes, celery, large pepper, and cucumbers; chop into little pieces.
Place in a large bowl and dress with oil, oregano, and a pinch of salt.
Mix and spoon onto the taralli on the plate.
Add wedges of hardboiled egg, the anchovies, and the olives.
Drizzle generously with oil and rest in the fridge 30 minutes before serving.
Boil the potatoes with their skin on; drain, peel when cool, and puree with a potato masher.
Simmer the nettles, drain, and cool; press out the water, mince, and stir into the mashed potatoes.
Add the egg yolk and a pinch of salt; mix well.
Stir in the flour until the mixture is uniform.
Shape the dough into "ropes" about 5 mm in diameter, then slice into pieces 1.5 cm long.
Clean the porcini with a damp cloth and cut into small chunks; sauté garlic in oil, add the porcini with salt, pepper, and a few tablespoons of water; cook on a low flame for 5 minutes.
Boil the gnocchi in lightly salted water; remove with a slotted spoon as soon as they float.
Toss with the porcini sauce and serve.

recipes.name_en: Octopus Salad with Potatoes and Green Beans
steps: Trim and clean the string beans; peel the potatoes; boil both in salted water.
In a deep pan coated in oil, heat the parsley minced with the garlic; add salt and pepper.
Drain the beans and potatoes while still firm and combine with the octopus cut into small pieces.
Dress with the sauce and serve warm.
Prepare the endive: cut into strips and soak in water for a few minutes.
Meanwhile, remove the heads of the anchovies, open them down the center, rinse, and dry.
Drain the endive and put a third in a deep pyriform dish; cover with half of the anchovies and dress with oil, garlic, salt, and pepper.
Make a second layer of endive, top with the rest of the anchovies, dress again, then cover with the remaining endive.
Bake at 200 °C for 30 minutes.
Serve warm, sprinkled with minced parsley.
Remove the skins of the fava beans.
Prepare the pesto by mashing the fava beans with the garlic (core removed), a few mint leaves, and a bit of oil.
Cook the linguine in well-salted boiling water; drain al dente, reserving some cooking water.
Toss the pasta with the pesto, loosening with reserved cooking water if too thick; serve.

recipes.name_en: Fava Beans with Garlic, Mint, and Chili Pepper
steps: Simmer the fava beans in very little unsalted water for 7–8 minutes; they should remain crunchy.
Drain and transfer to a large bowl.
Dress with a sauce made by mixing garlic with minced mint, oil, a dash of chili pepper, and salt.
Place the starch in a pot; slowly add the watermelon juice a little at a time, mixing constantly until smooth.
Add the sugar and continue mixing.
Cook on a medium flame, mixing constantly, until it comes to a boil.
Lower the flame and let the mixture thicken for a few minutes, mixing periodically.
Add the vanilla, cinnamon, and almost all the chocolate (reserve a few chips for garnish); mix one last time.
Pour into 6 dessert ramekins; sprinkle the remaining chocolate chips on top; refrigerate overnight.
Just before serving, sprinkle pistachio granules over each dessert.

recipes.name_en: Traditional Sicilian Pasta with Eggplant and Tomato Sauce
steps: Slice the eggplant and transfer to a bowl of salted water to draw out moisture.
Simmer the tomatoes, then peel and chop; cook on a low flame with the garlic in a terracotta pot.
Remove from the heat; stir in oil and basil.
Drain and dry the eggplant slices; grill them.
Cook the pasta in boiling water; drain and toss with the tomato sauce.
Plate with grilled eggplant slices; top with grated ricotta salata and more basil.
Toast the almonds.
Melt the chocolate in a bain-marie; add the almonds and mix.
Spoon the mixture into 20 ramekin dishes.
Let cool until the chocolate has solidified.
Cook the beans in a pressure pot: fill the pot to the level indicator, add a small handful of kosher salt, cook on the highest flame; once it whistles, lower to minimum and cook for 40 minutes.
Puree the beans with a vegetable mill or hand blender and transfer to a large pot.
Bring to a boil; add the onion (pierced with the cloves) and approximately 1 liter of water.
When the water reaches a boil, add the pasta; remove from the heat and stir periodically so the pasta does not stick.
Serve hot or warm; optionally add chopped Treviso red radicchio (bitter, aids digestion) or a tablespoon of trippe alla parmigiana for extra protein.
Finish with a drizzle of extra virgin olive oil, ground pepper, and a pinch of Franco's "magic powder" (dried sage, rosemary, thyme, marjoram).
Cook the polenta according to package instructions until soft.
Wash and cut the mushrooms; transfer to a pan with oil and a little water.
Cook over moderate heat, stirring often, until tender.
Add the chopped parsley.
Serve the polenta topped with the mushrooms.
Peel and clean the pumpkin; cut into slices 1 cm thick and place on a baking sheet.
Sprinkle with torn sage, rosemary, salt, and a little honey.
Bake at 140 °C for 30 minutes.

recipes.name_en: Chickpeas and Chestnuts with Rosemary and Garlic
steps: Soak the chickpeas overnight; reconstitute the dried chestnuts by soaking in warm water for 10 hours.
Boil the chickpeas for 2 hours.
Add the drained chestnuts, garlic, bay leaf, rosemary, oil, and a pinch of salt.
Cook for another 10 minutes or so, stirring regularly.
Clean the herbs and cut into small strips.
Finely slice the white part of the leeks and simmer on a low flame with oil and a bit of water.
Add the herbs and cook for 10 minutes.
Add the broth; when it comes to a boil, stir in the rice.
When the rice is cooked (about 40 minutes), stir in the minced parsley.
Serve, sprinkling with grated Grana Padano.

recipes.name_en: Pears Simmered in Spiced Red Wine
steps: Place all ingredients in a pot; bring to a boil.
Cook for 30–40 minutes until the liquid thickens.
Let cool, then remove the cinnamon stick and cloves.
Slice the pears and spoon the sauce over them; serve.

recipes.name_en: Corn Meal Porridge with Tuscan Black Cabbage
steps: Trim and wash the cabbage thoroughly, removing the hard ribs; cut into small strips.
Boil in about 5 liters of salted water; add the yellow corn meal a little at a time, stirring constantly with a whisk.
Cook for about 40 minutes, stirring periodically with a wooden spoon (do not scrape the bottom of the pot).
Add the minced garlic; taste and add salt as needed.
Add the oil and cheese; whisk together. The farinata should be less dense than polenta.
Serve hot, drizzling with raw oil and Parmigiano on the side.

recipes.name_en: 3-Flour Cake with Citrus Rind and Dried Fruit
steps: Combine the three flours, breadcrumbs, sugar, and a pinch of salt in a bowl; mix.
Add the milk and both oils; work the batter until smooth and uniform.
Peel the apples, cut into small pieces, and add to the mixture along with the grated rinds, raisins, and chopped figs.
Oil a 24 cm cake pan, dust with flour, and pour in the batter.
Bake at 170 °C for 45–50 minutes.
Let cool; serve, optionally sprinkled with powdered sugar.

recipes.name_en: Spiced Cake with Nuts, Chocolate, and Raisins
steps: Soak the raisins in warm water; drain and press dry.
Melt the cane sugar with a cup of water over a low flame.
Remove from the heat; add the dark chocolate and stir until melted.
Pour into a bowl; add the flour, nuts, raisins, a pinch of cinnamon and nutmeg, and a generous bit of ground pepper.
Let rest 30 minutes; preheat oven to 180 °C.
Spread the mixture on a baking sheet covered with wax paper, shaping into a loaf.
Bake 15 minutes; turn off the oven and leave the cake inside to cool.
The dessert is ready to eat the next day.
Clean the cauliflower and separate into florets.
Rinse and simmer in a small amount of water with a pinch of salt; the cauliflower should be al dente.
Drain and dress immediately with vinegar, oil, olives, capers, and the pepper cut into strips.

recipes.name_en: Corn Meal Cookies with Raisins, Dried Figs, and Nuts
steps: Soak the raisins in warm water.
Mince the walnuts and almonds with the dried figs.
Make a well with the corn meal; add a few tablespoons of oil, the drained raisins, the pine nuts, the minced figs, the sugar, and a pinch of salt and pepper.
Mix well, adding hot water to form a moist consistency.
Shape into balls, then flatten.
Bake at 150 °C; serve cold.
Soak the beans in cold water overnight; rinse, drain, and put in a pot with the carrot, onion, celery, bay leaf, and plenty of water.
Boil for an hour, adding salt towards the end.
In a casserole pot with a little water, simmer the radicchio for 5 minutes; drain off the water and chop finely.
Bring the broth to a boil; slowly sprinkle in the corn meal and mix.
After 10 minutes, add the beans and cook for 15 minutes.
Remove from the heat; stir in the radicchio with a bit of salt and pepper.
Pour into a soup tureen and serve.

recipes.name_en: Crostini with Artichoke-Stems and Shallot, Mint, Basil Sauce
steps: Clean and prepare the artichoke stems.
Soak them in acidified water (with lemon juice); dry and cut into cubes or julienne.
In a large pan with oil, sauté the sliced shallot, mint, basil, salt, and pepper.
Spoon the mixture onto the toasted bread and serve.
Peel the oranges; cut into thin slices and then small pieces, removing the seeds.
Transfer to a large bowl and dress with oil, the very thinly sliced chive bulb, a pinch of oregano, pepper, and salt.
Mix and let sit 15 minutes before serving.

recipes.name_en: Carrots with Pine Nuts and Wine-Seeped Raisins
steps: Soak the raisins in the wine.
Trim, peel, and clean the carrots; chop into rounds.
Simmer in oil, a small amount of water, and a pinch of salt; cover and cook slowly.
When tender, stir in the pine nuts and the drained raisins.
Mix well; cook until done and serve immediately.
